overview: This file documents the transition of U.S. economic policy toward Japan from wartime export restrictions to the practical provisioning and reconstruction of occupied Japan. Its principal focus is the disposal of U.S. military surplus through the Foreign Liquidation Commission, including interdepartmental debates over which goods could be sold, how Japanese purchases should be financed, and the agreements that ultimately authorized transfers of civilian-type equipment. It also covers essential imports such as fertilizer and raw fibers, administrative operations and expenses, and related questions involving trucks, communications equipment, surrendered supplies, vessels, and reparations. Although centered on 1945–1946, the file contains later material through 1949 that shows the longer aftermath of wartime property disposal and occupation policy.
interest: Shows occupation policy worked through mundane surplus decisions, turning $105 million of surplus into an instrument of Japanese stabilization.
